source: NCERT Class VII, Our Environment, Geography Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Forces that Change the Earth
points: **Endogenic (internal) forces** — act inside the Earth; can be **sudden** (earthquakes, volcanoes) or **slow**.
**Exogenic (external) forces** — act on the surface: **weathering and erosion** by rivers, wind, glaciers and sea waves.
Together these forces constantly **build up and wear down** the land.

sections.heading: 2. Lithospheric Plates, Earthquakes and Volcanoes
points: The Earth's crust is broken into **lithospheric plates** that move very slowly, changing the surface.
A **volcano** = a vent through which **molten magma** erupts onto the surface.
An **earthquake** = sudden shaking of the ground due to plate movement; the point of origin below the surface = **focus**; the point directly above on the surface = **epicentre**.
Earthquakes are measured by a **seismograph** (Richter scale).

sections.heading: 3. Weathering and Erosion
points: **Weathering** = the **breaking up** of rocks on the spot.
**Erosion** = the **wearing away and removal** of the land surface by agents (running water, wind, ice, waves).
**Deposition** = laying down of the eroded material — building new landforms.

sections.heading: 4. Landforms Made by Agents of Erosion/Deposition

sub: **Waterfall** (in the upper course); **meanders** (loops) and **ox-bow lakes**; **flood plains** and **levees**; a **delta** at the mouth.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Endogenic = internal (earthquakes, volcanoes); exogenic = external (weathering, erosion).
Earthquake: focus (origin below) & epicentre (point above); measured by seismograph.
River landforms: waterfall, meander, ox-bow lake, flood plain, delta.
Sea: caves→arches→stacks→cliffs, beaches; Glacier: U-valley, moraine; Wind: mushroom rock, dune, loess.
Weathering = breaking in place; erosion = wearing away & removal.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Focus** = point of origin **below** the surface; **epicentre** = point on the surface **directly above** the focus.
**Ox-bow lake** and **meander** are made by **rivers**; **loess** and **mushroom rocks** by **wind**.
A **delta** forms at a river's **mouth** (deposition); a **waterfall** in its **upper** course.
